areas.title: The audio chain: being heard and hearing
Crashes and performance, on web and native
Entry: dashboard, invite, admission, prejoin, embed and boot
Join and media connection, including listen-only
Platform: DB, releases, flags, Cloudflare edge
Report a problem and live introspection
Kernel self-tests. Test-only: never emitted in production, and left out of the Axiom schema and the CLI tables.

fields.name: admission
fields.doc: Whether an Episode admission was a direct admit or a knock.

fields.name: admission_request_id
fields.doc: The admission request.

fields.name: agent_id
fields.doc: The tenant's identifier for the agent.

fields.name: api_key_id
fields.doc: The API key row the request or decision names.

fields.name: api_start
fields.doc: Marks an api.starting row as an API start marker.

fields.name: api_version
fields.doc: The webhook payload version an endpoint revision requests.

fields.name: app_build
fields.doc: The host app's build number.

fields.name: app_version
fields.doc: The host app's version.

fields.name: attempt
fields.doc: Which run of a job or which try of an op this is, starting at 1.

fields.name: attempt_count
fields.doc: How many attempts the delivery has made.

fields.name: attempt_id
fields.doc: One webhook delivery attempt row.

fields.name: attempt_number
fields.doc: Which attempt of its delivery this row is, 1-based.

fields.name: attempt_outcome
fields.doc: The attempt's recorded outcome in webhook_delivery_attempts.

fields.name: auth_scheme
fields.doc: How the request authenticated: a tenant API key, a Dashboard session, a bearer grant, or nothing.

fields.name: banner_kind
fields.doc: Which self-test banner.

fields.name: batch_id
fields.doc: The batch that delivered the record. Stamped by the batcher or the ingest, not by the kernel.

fields.name: client_mono_ms
fields.doc: The client's monotonic clock, since its time origin.

fields.name: client_session_id
fields.doc: The SDK client session: one client object's lifetime. The client kernel stamps it on every record, separate from source_id, because one client session opens a new source for each Participant it joins as.

fields.name: client_wall_ms
fields.doc: The client's wall clock, in Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: clock_epoch
fields.doc: Counts clock jumps in this source. Records from different epochs are ordered only by seq.

fields.name: clock_err_ms
fields.doc: The bound on est_server_ms's error. Absent on server records.

fields.name: clock_state
fields.doc: Whether est_server_ms can be trusted.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: The API error code an access grant rejection carries.

fields.name: created_at_ms
fields.doc: When the row was created, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: credential_kind
fields.doc: The kind of credential tenant.authorize checked.

fields.name: current
fields.doc: Whether this revision is the endpoint's current one.

fields.name: deadline_at_ms
fields.doc: When the Episode's deadline scheduler was due to end it, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: decision
fields.doc: What a decision decided, from the event's declared values.

fields.name: decision_id
fields.doc: The decision.

fields.name: deleted_at_ms
fields.doc: When the row was deleted, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: delivery_state
fields.doc: The delivery's state in webhook_deliveries.

fields.name: device_ephemeral
fields.doc: True when device_id could not be stored and lives only for this client session.

fields.name: device_id
fields.doc: The persistent device.

fields.name: drop_reason
fields.doc: On a drop record (C3): why the client gave up on the seqs in dropped_seqs.

fields.name: dropped_seqs
fields.doc: On a drop record (C3): the half-open seq ranges [from, to) of the record's own source that the client gave up on, all below the record's seq, at most 64.

fields.name: duration_ms
fields.doc: An op's duration, or how long a state lasted.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether the endpoint row was enabled at the snapshot time.

fields.name: end
fields.doc: How a source ended (C3), on the batch that reports it: closed (the client said its last next_seq exactly) or abandoned (the next page load found it dead and reports the last high-water mark it persisted). The ledger refuses an end below a seq it settled or below a next_seq already reported, so the missing suffix stays a gap.

fields.name: end_reason
fields.doc: Why a call or an Episode ended. The server and the client use different values, so each event narrows the list.

fields.name: ended_at_ms
fields.doc: When the Episode ended, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: env
fields.doc: The environment.

fields.name: episode_id
fields.doc: The Episode.

fields.name: error_class
fields.doc: The bounded class of a cycle failure error, never its text.

fields.name: error_code
fields.doc: The delivery or request error code; see the delivery client's bounded vocabulary and the API's public error codes.

fields.name: est_server_ms
fields.doc: The estimated server time in Unix milliseconds. A server stamps its own clock.

fields.name: event_id
fields.doc: One record. Minted by the kernel when the record is made.

fields.name: event_name
fields.doc: The webhook event name a lifecycle transition commits or a subscription lists.

fields.name: finished_at_ms
fields.doc: When an attempt finished, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: The full flags map: config switches, the media-plane kill switch and caps. Never credentials.

fields.name: flags_hash
fields.doc: 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the canonical flags JSON. Resolve it with the obs.flags_snapshot fact that carries the same hash.

fields.name: from_state
fields.doc: The state before a transition.

fields.name: generation
fields.doc: Which join of the Participant seat this is.

fields.name: grant_kind
fields.doc: Whether an issueAccessGrant call was a Participant's first grant or a media-token renewal.

fields.name: host_boot_id
fields.doc: The host boot identity the API start marker carries.

fields.name: http_status
fields.doc: The HTTP status the receiver answered.

fields.name: http_status_class
fields.doc: The class of the receiver's HTTP status; none when no response arrived.

fields.name: immediate
fields.doc: Whether the secret rotation took effect at once, dropping the grace period.

fields.name: item_count
fields.doc: How many items a self-test op handled.

fields.name: job_id
fields.doc: The background job.

fields.name: joined_at_ms
fields.doc: When the Participant joined, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: journey_id
fields.doc: The user-visible attempt this record belongs to.

fields.name: jump_ms
fields.doc: How far the wall clock stepped against the monotonic clock.

fields.name: key_created_ms
fields.doc: When the API key row was created, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: key_expires_at_ms
fields.doc: When the API key expires, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: key_prefix
fields.doc: The lookup prefix of an API key; a lookup index, never the secret.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: op, transition, decision, surface or fact.

fields.name: last_used_at_ms
fields.doc: When the API key last authenticated successfully, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: latency_milliseconds
fields.doc: The receiver round-trip time recorded on the attempt.

fields.name: lease_expires_at_ms
fields.doc: When the delivering claim's lease expires, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: left_at_ms
fields.doc: When the Participant left, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: The configured live Episode limit the decision enforced.

fields.name: live_count
fields.doc: The live Episode count the live-limit decision counted.

fields.name: machine
fields.doc: A transition's machine.

fields.name: media_connection_id
fields.doc: Chalk's media connection.

fields.name: method
fields.doc: The HTTP method of a request.

fields.name: module
fields.doc: The emitting program.

fields.name: mutation_created_ms
fields.doc: When the API key mutation request row was created, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: mutation_kind
fields.doc: The API key mutation an api_key_mutation_requests row records.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The registry event name. A transition's name is its machine.

fields.name: next_attempt_at_ms
fields.doc: When the delivery is next scheduled, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: next_seq
fields.doc: The source's high-water mark on every batch (C3): every seq below it has been assigned.

fields.name: note_kind
fields.doc: Which self-test note.

fields.name: occurred_at_ms
fields.doc: When the event or transition occurred, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: op_id
fields.doc: The op.

fields.name: outcome
fields.doc: An op's terminal outcome.

fields.name: parent_delivery_id
fields.doc: The delivery an erased delivery's redelivery names as parent.

fields.name: parent_op_id
fields.doc: The op that started this one.

fields.name: participant_id
fields.doc: The Participant seat in the Episode.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: The URL path of a request; ids in it are the resource ids the route acts on.

fields.name: platform
fields.doc: Where the program runs.

fields.name: policy
fields.doc: The rate-limit policy name that refused the request.

fields.name: previous_boot_end_ms
fields.doc: When this host's previous boot's log ended, Unix milliseconds; null when unknown.

fields.name: previous_secret_expires_at_ms
fields.doc: When a rotated webhook endpoint's previous secret stopped being valid, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: provider_media_id
fields.doc: The media provider's session id.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: The bounded stage an access grant rejection names.

fields.name: reason_code
fields.doc: A registry reason code. Required when the outcome is expected or error, and on a decision that refuses, times out, closes or limits.

fields.name: recording_id
fields.doc: The recording.

fields.name: release_sha
fields.doc: The git commit the program was built from.

fields.name: request_id
fields.doc: The request attempt.

fields.name: request_logs
fields.doc: The API request-log mode the process booted with.

fields.name: required_scope
fields.doc: The scope tenant.authorize required and the credential lacked.

fields.name: resource_id
fields.doc: The id of the resource a webhook event is about: a Space, Episode, Participant or endpoint id.

fields.name: resource_type
fields.doc: The kind of resource a webhook event is about.

fields.name: retry_after_ms
fields.doc: The Retry-After the rate-limit refusal sent, in milliseconds.

fields.name: revoked_at_ms
fields.doc: When the API key was revoked, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: route
fields.doc: The matched route pattern of an HTTP request, such as createEpisode.

fields.name: schema_ver
fields.doc: The registry's content hash, so a reader knows which catalogue the record was written against.

fields.name: scopes
fields.doc: The API key's scopes, comma-separated.

fields.name: sdk_version
fields.doc: The Chalk SDK version inside the host app.

fields.name: semantic_transition_key
fields.doc: The dedupe key a webhook event row carries for its semantic transition.

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: The record's position in its source's stream, with no reuse. On a client the outbox stamps it, never the kernel. A client source counts from 0, as the outbox and the delivery ledger do (C3); a server source (the API, SFU and Sync kernels) counts from 1 and has no ledger.

fields.name: shown_ms
fields.doc: How long a dismissed surface was on screen.

fields.name: source_id
fields.doc: The stream that owns seq. On a client the outbox stamps it with seq. A client starts a new source for each page load and for each Participant it joins as, and only that Participant's credential may write it (C3); a server uses its instance id.

fields.name: space_id
fields.doc: The Space.

fields.name: span_id
fields.doc: The W3C span.

fields.name: stage
fields.doc: Which part of a dispatcher cycle failed.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.doc: When an attempt, Episode or boot started, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: The HTTP status the API answered.

fields.name: subscribed
fields.doc: The event names the endpoint revision subscribed to, comma-separated.

fields.name: surface_state
fields.doc: Whether a surface was shown or dismissed.

fields.name: sync_connection_id
fields.doc: The Sync websocket.

fields.name: target_count
fields.doc: How many endpoint targets a fanout decision committed.

fields.name: tenant_id
fields.doc: The tenant.

fields.name: terminal_at_ms
fields.doc: When the delivery reached a terminal state, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: to_state
fields.doc: The state after a transition.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: The W3C trace.

fields.name: trigger
fields.doc: What caused a transition, from the machine's trigger list.

fields.name: updated_at_ms
fields.doc: When the row was last updated, Unix milliseconds.

fields.name: user_id
fields.doc: The tenant's identifier for the person.

fields.name: webhook_delivery_id
fields.doc: The webhook delivery.

fields.name: webhook_endpoint_id
fields.doc: The webhook endpoint.

fields.name: webhook_event_id
fields.doc: The committed webhook_events row.

reasons.doc: The caller cancelled the operation before it finished.
The Episode reached its time limit and the API ended it. The client failures the end itself caused are expected.
The Episode's capacity refused the admission.
The Episode had already ended when the admission was refused.
The Episode held at least 500 live Participants, so its capacity refused the admission.
The rate limiter's token bucket was empty, so the request was refused 429.
The API key was past its expiry.
The key's secret did not match the stored hash.
The rate limiter could not answer, so the request was refused 503.
The Tenant was at its live Episode limit and every counted Episode was still live.
The Tenant's live Episode limit refused the create.
The API key lookup failed inside the API.
The presented credential was not a parseable API key.
The API key was revoked.
The credential lacks the scope the route needs.
The API key's stored scopes failed validation inside the API.
The credential belongs to a different Tenant than the path's.
The key's prefix matched no API key row.
A self-test error.
A self-test expected outcome.
An error that no classifier named. Counted as unexplained, so a rise is a gap in the catalogue.
The attempt's trace link could not be recorded, so the attempt did not start.
The attempt's outcome write did not commit.
The TCP connection to the receiver failed.
A deploy restarted the API while the attempt ran, so its outcome was never recorded.
The receiver's host name did not resolve.
The URL or secret ciphertext could not be unprotected.
The receiver answered a non-success 2xx status, which the delivery client does not accept.
The receiver answered a redirect; the delivery client does not follow it.
The receiver refused the signed request.
The receiver failed the request; the delivery retries.
The receiver answered a status outside 100-599.
The attempt's lease expired before its outcome committed.
The delivery's lease was lost while the attempt completed.
The request failed on the network.
No endpoint of the Tenant was enabled, current and subscribed to the event at the transition.
A delivery error outside the bounded vocabulary.
The endpoint or the Tenant's concurrency budget stayed saturated by slow in-flight attempts for the whole wait.
The delivery request could not be built.
The receiver's response headers exceeded the bound.
The receiver's response body exceeded the bound.
The delivery passed the 72 h horizon without a terminal state.
The endpoint's secret rotated while the attempt was in flight.
The endpoint URL resolved to an address delivery refuses.
The receiver did not answer in time.
The TLS handshake with the receiver failed.
The endpoint URL is not one the delivery client will call.

events.name: api.api_key.authenticate
events.doc: An API key presented on a request was authenticated. Rejected names why the credential was refused.

events.name: api.episode.admission.capacity
events.doc: The Episode's capacity check refused an admission, recorded for refusals only. The query can't say which limit failed; the checker counts Participants itself.

events.name: api.episode.create.live_limit
events.doc: The Tenant's live Episode limit refused an Episode creation, recorded for refusals only.

events.name: api.ratelimit.check
events.doc: A write or read policy's check decided the request, accepted or refused.

events.name: api.tenant.authorize
events.doc: A credential was refused authorization for the Tenant in its path, recorded for refusals only.

events.name: api.webhook.delivery.attempt
events.doc: One delivery attempt the dispatcher ran, ending ok on a 2xx or error(<code>) otherwise.

events.name: api.webhook.dispatch.cycle_failed
events.doc: One dispatcher cycle stage failed. Loop-level failures carry no Tenant; claim-stage ones do.

events.name: api.webhook.endpoint.secret_rotated
events.doc: An endpoint's signing secret rotated, emitted after the rotation commit.

events.name: api.webhook.event.fanout
events.doc: The API's webhook producer ran after the transition's commit and recorded what it wrote to webhook_events.

events.name: client.call_ended
events.doc: The SDK decided which end screen the call gets. The client kernel records it where the connection chooses the end screen, and the API logs it as a kernel row. An SDK release before the client kernel sent it as an sdk.telemetry row of type call_ended, which the legacy match still reads.

events.name: integration.db.api_key
events.doc: One api_keys row the revoke route owns, read by the checker. The secret hash is never read.

events.name: integration.db.key_mutation
events.doc: One api_key_mutation_requests row: a create or rotate the Tenant ran.

events.name: integration.log.grant_rejected
events.doc: An access_grant.rejected request-log row: an issueAccessGrant call refused, with its grant kind.

events.name: integration.log.http_request
events.doc: One http.request request-log row, with the auth principal the middleware recorded.

events.name: obs.clock_jump
events.doc: The client's wall clock stepped, so its clock samples were dropped and clock_epoch moved on.

events.name: obs.flags_snapshot
events.doc: The full flags map behind the flags_hash the kernel stamps on this and every later record. Logged at boot, at join and whenever the flags change.

events.name: selftest.admit
events.doc: A self-test decision.

events.name: selftest.banner
events.doc: A self-test surface.

events.name: selftest.note
events.doc: A self-test fact.

events.name: selftest.work
events.doc: A self-test op.

events.name: sync.episode.ended
events.doc: Sync saw the Episode's authoritative end, with the reason the API stored in episodes.end_reason.

events.name: webhook.db.attempt
events.doc: One webhook_delivery_attempts row, read by the checker.

events.name: webhook.db.delivery
events.doc: One webhook_deliveries row joined to its event, read by the checker.

events.name: webhook.db.endpoint
events.doc: An endpoint row's state at one revision, with the window it was current from, read by the checker.

events.name: webhook.db.episode
events.doc: One episodes row the checker counts for live-limit, capacity and create-refusal evidence.

events.name: webhook.db.event
events.doc: One committed webhook_events row, read by the checker.

events.name: webhook.db.lifecycle
events.doc: One lifecycle transition in Postgres: an Episode's start or end, a Participant's join or leave, read by the checker.

events.name: webhook.db.participant
events.doc: One participants row the checker counts for capacity and admission-retry evidence.

events.name: webhook.db.retry
events.doc: A webhook.delivery.retry_scheduled journey-ledger row, with the next_attempt_at the scheduler wrote.

events.name: webhook.db.space
events.doc: One spaces row, create-refusal evidence the checker reads.

events.name: webhook.log.api_start
events.doc: The API's start marker, projected from the api.starting log row. Until slice 14's release markers land it is this slice's restart witness, and it carries the request_log mode.

events.name: webhook.log.complete_failed
events.doc: The dispatcher's completion-failed log for an attempt whose terminal write did not commit.

machines.name: client.connection
machines.doc: The SDK connection state (CONNECTION_STATES in sdks/typescript/client/src/connection/types.ts). Its one writer is transition() in connection/lifecycle.ts.

machines.name: episode.lifecycle
machines.doc: The Episode row's status in Postgres (episodes.status).

facts.name: admission.decision
facts.doc: The API's admission decision for a join attempt. Claim: admitted, or the refusal reason.

facts.name: audio.capture
facts.doc: A rollup of a seat's microphone level before WebRTC over exactly its window. Values: rms_max_dbfs.

facts.name: audio.ingress
facts.doc: A rollup of a seat's audio packets at SFU ingress over exactly its window. Values: packets, voiced.

facts.name: audio.mic_state
facts.doc: Whether a seat's microphone was muted or unmuted, held over a window. Claim: muted or unmuted.

facts.name: board.camera
facts.doc: One move of a viewer's board camera. Claim: what moved it (user_pan, follow, fit and so on).

facts.name: end.client_screen
facts.doc: The end screen a client chose for its call. Claim: the client's end reason. A failure screen (connection lost, join failed) is a failure some finding must explain.

facts.name: end.episode
facts.doc: The Episode's authoritative end. Claim: the end reason.

facts.name: integration.api_key
facts.doc: An api_keys row: revocation, expiry and last success, independent of the auth decision because the revoke route writes it.

facts.name: integration.auth
facts.doc: An api_key.authenticate decision: accepted or refused with its reason.

facts.name: integration.authorize
facts.doc: A tenant.authorize refusal: the scope the credential lacked or the Tenant it mismatched.

facts.name: integration.capacity
facts.doc: An episode.admission.capacity refusal and whether the admission was direct or a knock.

facts.name: integration.grant_rejected
facts.doc: An access_grant.rejected row: an issueAccessGrant refusal and its grant kind.

facts.name: integration.key_mutation
facts.doc: A create or rotate the Tenant ran on its API keys; the rotation witness behind the unknown_prefix hypothesis.

facts.name: integration.live_limit
facts.doc: An episode.create.live_limit refusal and the live count it enforced.

facts.name: integration.rate_limit
facts.doc: A ratelimit.check refusal and the policy that refused it.

facts.name: integration.request
facts.doc: An http.request row: the request, its status and the principal that presented.

facts.name: integration.request_log_mode
facts.doc: The request-log mode the API booted with, until C1's obs.flags_snapshot carries it for every record.

facts.name: join.leave
facts.doc: A seat's leave request and its outcome. A failed leave is a failure every finding must account for.

facts.name: recording.job_state
facts.doc: The terminal state of a post-call job, read from its Postgres row. Claim: succeeded or the failure state.

facts.name: report.problem
facts.doc: A problem report a person filed, from a seat or from outside the call. Claim: the report kind.

facts.name: webhook.attempt
facts.doc: A webhook_delivery_attempts row: the attempt's outcome, status and timing.

facts.name: webhook.attempt_op
facts.doc: The dispatcher's attempt op, the in-flight witness beside the attempt table row.

facts.name: webhook.complete_failed
facts.doc: A completion-failed dispatcher log for one attempt, with the status class the receiver had answered.

facts.name: webhook.cycle
facts.doc: A dispatcher cycle failure, by stage. Loop-level failures carry no Tenant; the checker's reader joins them to the Tenant day.

facts.name: webhook.delivery
facts.doc: A webhook_deliveries row: its state, schedule, lease and attempt count.

facts.name: webhook.endpoint
facts.doc: An endpoint's enable, delete and subscription state at a revision, so the rule can tell whether an endpoint subscribed at the transition.

facts.name: webhook.episode
facts.doc: An episodes row for the checker's own counts: live-limit, capacity and create-refusal evidence.

facts.name: webhook.event
facts.doc: A committed webhook_events row for the Tenant.

facts.name: webhook.fanout
facts.doc: The API producer's fanout decision for one transition: committed, duplicate or no_targets.

facts.name: webhook.marker
facts.doc: An API start marker. Until slice 14's release.marker lands, the api.starting row is the deploy-restart witness; a complete api-source window with no marker proves no restart.

facts.name: webhook.participant
facts.doc: A participants row for capacity and admission-retry counts.

facts.name: webhook.retry
facts.doc: A retry_scheduled ledger row with the next_attempt_at the scheduler set.

facts.name: webhook.secret_rotation
facts.doc: An endpoint secret rotation, the witness that falsifies a stale-secret hypothesis.

facts.name: webhook.space
facts.doc: A spaces row, the createSpace success the checker counts.

facts.name: webhook.transition
facts.doc: A lifecycle transition a subscribed endpoint should hear about: episode.started, episode.ended, participant.joined or participant.left, from the authoritative Postgres rows.

symptoms.doc: The client lost its connection and did not recover within the recovery window.
A join attempt never got an admission decision, so the person waited on a screen that never resolved.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where client_session_id == '{attempt}' and kind == 'decision' and name in ('invite.resolve', 'admission.decided')
witnesses.doc: The decision that admits or refuses the attempt.

symptoms.doc: The Participant can't hear someone who is speaking.
The Participant's microphone is on but others can't hear them.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and event == 'sdk.mic_state' | where _time between (datetime({from}) .. datetime({to}))
witnesses.doc: When the seat's microphone was unmuted.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and event == 'sfu.media.ingress' and media_kind == 'audio' | where _time between (datetime({from}) .. datetime({to}))
witnesses.doc: Whether voiced packets reached the SFU while it was unmuted.
The capture level, which attributes a silent ingress to a client hop.

symptoms.doc: A follower's whiteboard view jumped away from what the person they follow is looking at.

witnesses.doc: Every camera move, so a burst of automatic moves shows.

symptoms.doc: The Episode reached its time limit and ended. Expected, and it claims the client failures the end itself caused.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'sync.episode.ended'
witnesses.doc: The authoritative end Sync saw, with the reason the API stored. A time-limit end has the reason maximum_duration.

symptoms.doc: The Episode ended for an authoritative reason, but the client showed a failure end screen (connection lost or join failed) instead of the Episode-ended screen.
user_words: it said I lost connection when the class ended
the call ended with an error

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and name == 'sync.episode.ended'
witnesses.doc: The authoritative end and when it happened.

witnesses.query: axiom chalk-logs | where episode_id == '{episode}' and participant_id == '{participant}' and (name == 'client.call_ended' or (event == 'sdk.telemetry' and type == 'call_ended'))
witnesses.doc: The end screen the seat's client chose.

symptoms.doc: API-key requests were refused and the Tenant had no API-key success within 5 min after the first refusal.

witnesses.doc: Authenticate decisions, the refusal and the success witness.
Request rows with auth_scheme; a 2xx by api_key is a second success witness.
Revocation, expiry and last_used_at, independent of the decision.
Whether request rows exist at all for the window.
Authorization refusals, a refusal witness when auth passed.
Rotations behind the unknown_prefix hypothesis.

symptoms.doc: A createSpace or createEpisode call was refused or failed and no Space or Episode in the same Space followed within 60 s.

witnesses.doc: The refused create requests and any 2xx retry.
Space rows the checker counts itself.
Episode rows: create evidence, live-limit count, deadline leaks.
The live-limit decision for tenant.live_episode_limit_reached refusals.
Whether counted Episodes still held live Participants.

symptoms.doc: An admitEpisodeParticipant or initial issueAccessGrant was refused or failed and was not retried successfully within 120 s.
user_words: participants can't get into the episode

witnesses.doc: The refused admissions and grants, plus 2xx retries.
Grant refusals with their grant kind.
Rate-limit refusals and Retry-After.
Whether all write requests were counted; a 429 under lesser logging is a gap.
Participants created in the retry window, and the 500-live-Participant count.
Whether the Episode had ended when the admission was refused.
The capacity refusal decision.
Key rows, to group refusals by caller.

symptoms.doc: The Participant joined but no media connected, so they neither hear nor are heard.
The call page crashed or rendered an error boundary.
An ended Episode's recording never became ready to watch.

witnesses.query: postgres: select state, updated_at from recording_jobs where id = '{job}'
witnesses.doc: Whether and how the job ended.

symptoms.doc: A Participant who left or dropped could not rejoin an Episode that was still active.
user_words: it won't let me back in

symptoms.doc: The Participant stopped sharing but others still see the share.
user_words: my screen is still being shared

symptoms.doc: A video tile stopped updating while its publisher was still sending.
A delivery waits in pending or retry_wait more than 120 s past its scheduled time, or sits delivering past a 60 s-expired lease.
user_words: deliveries are queued but nothing sends

witnesses.doc: Delivery states, schedules and leases.
When attempts started and finished, for the wait and the receiver-slow count.

witnesses.query: postgres observability_journey_events | where tenant_id == '{tenant}' and kind == 'webhook.delivery.retry_scheduled'
witnesses.doc: The scheduled retry time the ledger recorded.
Dispatcher loop failures; absence on a covered window proves the loop ran.
API start markers; a restart moves the stall's start. Incomplete coverage is the gap.

symptoms.doc: A lifecycle transition in the last 30 days, older than 30 s, has no matching webhook_events row although an endpoint subscribed (or the event is written unconditionally).
user_words: our webhook endpoint never got the event
an episode started and we heard nothing

witnesses.query: postgres webhook transitions | where tenant_id == '{tenant}' and occurred_at_ms >= {from} and occurred_at_ms <= {to}
witnesses.doc: The lifecycle transition population from episodes and participants.

witnesses.query: postgres webhook_events | where tenant_id == '{tenant}' and occurred_at >= {from}
witnesses.doc: The committed event rows the transitions should match.
Which endpoints were enabled and subscribed when.

witnesses.query: api log | where name == 'api.webhook.event.fanout' and tenant_id == '{tenant}'
witnesses.doc: The producer's own decisions; a duplicate decision prints as a fact.

symptoms.doc: A delivery exhausted its attempts. The last attempt's code says whether the Tenant's receiver refused it, could not be reached, or the API failed it.

witnesses.doc: The exhausted deliveries.
The attempts' statuses and error codes.

witnesses.query: api log | where name == 'api.webhook.endpoint.secret_rotated' and tenant_id == '{tenant}'
witnesses.doc: Rotations that falsify the stale-secret hypothesis.

symptoms.doc: An attempt's outcome was never recorded (outcome=lease_expired): the receiver's answer is unknown and a redelivery may duplicate.
user_words: did you deliver that event or not

witnesses.query: postgres webhook_delivery_attempts | where tenant_id == '{tenant}' and attempt_outcome == 'lease_expired'
witnesses.doc: The lease_expired attempt population.
The dispatcher's op, which may still know the receiver's answer.
The completion-failed log, with the status class.
A restart inside the attempt window explains the lost outcome.
